newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bullish Wall St chases Singapore stock blues away.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Wall St chases Singapore stock blues away.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was boosted on Thursday by a Wall Street enthused by electronics shares and some small-capitalised stocks and electronics counters hit new highs, dealers said.

"Interest in blue chips was thin. It's mainly the electronic counters moving up along with Wall Street. Also, with Malaysia on holiday, the poor sentiment plaguing the market recently due to the weak ringgit was removed. That helped," said one.
The SES electronics index surged 2.45 percent, or 3.36 points, to end at 140.24 after Nasdaq posted a record 38.52 point rally to an unofficial close of 1,580.63.
The SES index was pulled up by multimedia Creative Technology, which rose 90 cents to hit a three-year high of Singapore $32.80 as analysts remained optimistic about its earnings prospects.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 2.65 points up at 1,920.54.
Dealers said interest was seen from retail and institutional investors. Foreign interest was also evident, notably in the U.S.-denominated stocks as the Singapore dollar weakened.
"Two years ago, nobody was interested in these stocks, but the strength of the dollar around the region has pushed up interest in the U.S-denominated stocks," a dealer with a local bank said.

The Singapore dollar fell to a 30-month low of 1.4593 on Thursday as U.S. funds continued to dump the local currency for the U.S. dollar. The Singapore dollar was seen adjusting to recent losses on the Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah.
Book publisher Popular and Chinese drug company Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical were responsible for a fifth of the total market turnover of 244.96 million shares.
More than 47.9 million shares in the two companies were traded after buy recommendations by research houses.
